claims.text: Rapid thermal synthesis causes nucleation to outpace atomic diffusion in noble-metal HEA nanoparticles.
Limited diffusion produces local composition fluctuations that promote phase separation and elemental segregation.
An intermediate-temperature dwell provides additional time for atomic diffusion.
Dwell-enhanced diffusion makes elemental mixing more uniform and stabilizes a single-phase solid solution.
The nanoparticles are synthesized from a solid, single-source multimetal precursor.
Incomplete diffusion in the initial state causes phase separation, Pt-rich nucleation centers, and structural defects.
The relevant dwell-temperature window lies between initial crystallization at about 170 °C and complete precursor decomposition at about 230 °C.
The cited in situ XRD/XAS observations establish the approximately 170–230 °C temperature window.
The elements in the multimetal precursor reduce sequentially rather than cooperatively.
Early Pt reduction creates Pt-rich nuclei and localized composition fluctuations.
The dwell reduces local concentration gradients through interdiffusion between nucleated metallic clusters.
Cooling after the dwell kinetically traps a more homogeneous single-phase crystalline lattice.
Relative to synthesis without a dwell, the dwell-treated nanoparticles will have a more homogeneous elemental distribution.
Relative to synthesis without a dwell, the dwell-treated nanoparticles will show less phase separation and elemental segregation.
Relative to synthesis without a dwell, the dwell-treated nanoparticles will have fewer structural defects, including fewer stacking faults.
Relative to synthesis without a dwell, the dwell-treated nanoparticles will have a purer single-phase crystal structure.
Baseline rapid synthesis without a dwell exhibits phase separation, localized segregation, and high defect density because interdiffusion is inadequate.
The mechanism applies to nanoparticles containing more than five noble-metal elements under rapid thermal processing.
An excessively long dwell may cause particle overgrowth or sintering.

contradictions.description: The stated scope requires more than five elements, but the only explicit example lists Pt, Ir, Rh, Os, and Ru, which is exactly five elements.
